doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: How Armstrong learned so much music; origin of scat
summary: Jacobs says music came effortlessly to Louis, who put his horn first, and describes how scat started when he lost the music.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Switching subjects a little bit, perhaps you can, Phoebe you can help me out with this, you know I’ve been looking through a seemingly endless supply of Louis Armstrong records and I often wondered how did he learn so many songs to be — how did he record so much music? Did you ever witness him learning?

Yes. I witnessed Louis learning. Louis’ life was music. His dedication and his passion was performing. He lived to entertain people. It was effortless for him. It was like breathing. He told his wife Lucille, who he adored, you’ve got to understand, Mama, my horn comes first, and she understood and she never was jealous of his horn. But that was Louis. It was effortless for him to learn. But he’d go in a place, well that’s how scat singing started, because he lost the music that was on the music stand but he didn’t want to stop. He told the engineer to keep going and he just did his thing and he started scatting.
Would he sit with the pianist perhaps and learn the tune that way?
